contracts.commit_point: The awaited call main_agent.commit_session_memory(...) inside _maybe_commit_session (chat.py:34), through which all three triggers funnel before the session is removed from the activity table.
contracts.declared_mechanism: Three-trigger commit guard in gis_agent/API/chat.py: (1) explicit endpoint POST /api/chat/commit which commits and then pops the session from _session_activity to prevent duplicate commits (chat.py:150-162); (2) new-session trigger in guard_commit_on_new_request comparing _last_session_id (chat.py:54-58); (3) inactivity timeout trigger scanning _session_activity against _MEMORY_COMMIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, default 30 minutes (chat.py:22, 48-52); the guard is invoked at the entry of /api/chat (chat.py:70) and /api/chat/stream (chat.py:109) before the conversation executes.
contracts.forbidden_condition: Premature persistence of an in-progress (not yet ended) session's conversation into long-term memory — per the endpoint contract, writing 'Semi-finished products' (half-finished results) or pre-retraction incorrect facts — and duplicate re-commit of the same session segment after it has already been committed.
pending_binding_information: Implementation of MainAgent.commit_session_memory: the backing store type (database / file / external service) needed to confirm the effect_stratum, and whether the persisted content includes agent-generated messages.
Whether MainAgent also triggers memory commits internally during agent execution (which would establish an agent lifecycle binding) — not visible in supplied source.
Whether MainAgent.get_stream requests share the SupervisorGraph/guardrail path (MainAgent implementation not supplied).
Deployed value of MEMORY_COMMIT_TIMEOUT_MINUTES and whether deployment is single-process as the guard's comments assume.
contracts.protected_operation: Long-term-memory persistence of a session: main_agent.commit_session_memory(session_id, user_id), declared to perform extraction + dedup + persistence of the session conversation.
contracts.protected_resource: Per-session long-term memory records keyed by (session_id, user_id) written through MainAgent.commit_session_memory.
contracts.protection_obligation: Session conversation data may be persisted to long-term memory only at session end via the declared 'Three insurances' (three-insurance) commit guard — an explicit POST /api/chat/commit call, a new-session switch, or an inactivity timeout; in-progress sessions must not be committed (avoiding half-finished answers or facts the user retracted entering long-term memory), and an already-committed session segment must not be re-committed. (Raised as a secondary guard in the second-phase reviewer rationale; compiled separately as a distinct source-supported obligation.)
scope_limits: Guard state (_session_activity, _last_session_id, timeout constant) is in-process module-level state; the source comments state this is sufficient only for single-process deployment and that multi-worker deployments need shared storage such as Redis (chat.py:19-24).
Commit failures are silently swallowed: _maybe_commit_session logs a warning and returns 0 without retry or blocking (chat.py:31-40).

The guard only creates commit triggers; it does not veto any persistence call — the explicit /api/chat/commit endpoint commits whatever session_id it receives, and avoiding in-progress commits relies on the frontend calling it only at conversation end (chat.py:152-156).
The timeout sweep deliberately skips the currently active session (sid != session_id, chat.py:49-52).

The persistence target implementation (MainAgent.commit_session_memory) is not in the supplied views; the 'database' stratum is provisional pending confirmation of the backing store (could be file or external service).

Agent mediation is not established: the commit is invoked from HTTP request handlers, not from a shown agent tool call or lifecycle hook, and the dataflow of agent-generated content into the persisted record lies inside the unsupplied MainAgent.

contracts.commit_point: Evaluation of the route_after_guardrail conditional edge after guardrail_check completes: when state.guardrail_blocked is True the graph commits to END (run terminates before the supervisor node executes); otherwise it commits to the supervisor node (guardrail.py:198-200, wired at supervisor_graph.py:184-188).
contracts.declared_mechanism: LangGraph input-side guardrail node: SupervisorGraph._build_graph registers guardrail_check via builder.add_node and wires START -> guardrail_check -> conditional edges (route_after_guardrail) that map guardrail_blocked=True to END and otherwise to 'supervisor' (supervisor_graph.py:180-188). The guard uses a separate GLM-4-Flash model (temperature=0, _mode, Pydantic-validated JailbreakOutput with one retry) isolated from the main Qwen chain, declared as model-diversity defense; the module docstring declares a fail-open error policy.
contracts.forbidden_condition: A user message classified as jailbreak/prompt-injection (JailbreakOutput.is_safe == False: attempts to bypass or override system instructions/policy, extract system prompts or internal data, 'ignore all instructions above', SQL-injection fragments, unlimited-AI role-play, smuggled code/instruction sequences) proceeding past the guardrail into the supervisor node of the graph instead of terminating at END.
pending_binding_information: Whether MainAgent.get_stream (chat.py:75-79, 113-117) invokes SupervisorGraph, or another graph that includes guardrail_check — the MainAgent implementation is not in the supplied views.
Runtime values of settings.guardrail_enabled, guardrail_check_relevance, guardrail_block_irrelevant, and presence of zhipu_api_key (config module not supplied).
Whether any other invocation path can reach the supervisor node without passing START -> guardrail_check (e.g., single-agent mode mentioned in supervisor_graph.py:7).
Whether the END short-circuit also prevents subsequent turns served from the MemorySaver checkpointer from re-driving previously blocked input, given that only the latest message is re-checked.
contracts.protected_operation: Execution of the SupervisorGraph agent chain on user input — the supervisor routing decision (supervisor_decision node) and the downstream sub-agent nodes (data/knowledge/spatial/general) with their tool calls — which is declared to run only on input that passed the guardrail.
contracts.protected_resource: The supervisor multi-agent graph main chain (supervisor node plus DATA/KNOWLEDGE/SPATIAL/GENERAL worker nodes) declared in gis_agent/agent/multi_agent/supervisor_graph.py.
contracts.protection_obligation: Jailbreak / prompt-injection user messages must be intercepted at the entry of the supervisor multi-agent graph: the guardrail_check node classifies the latest user message, and on an unsafe (jailbreak/injection) verdict sets guardrail_blocked=True so that route_after_guardrail short-circuits the run to END, so that such input does not drive the supervisor decision or its downstream worker/tool chain. (Merged from both first- and second-phase reviewer wordings, which state the same obligation.)
scope_limits: Fail-open policy as declared in source: missing ZHIPU_API_KEY, guardrail model initialization failure, or classification-call failure all return guardrail_blocked=False and let the input through (guardrail.py:14-16, 146-154, 162-164); only an affirmative unsafe verdict blocks.
Master switch settings.guardrail_enabled=False disables the check entirely (guardrail.py:136-138); enforcement therefore depends on configuration values not present in supplied source.
Only the latest HumanMessage is classified; earlier history is assumed already vetted (guardrail.py:140-144).

The domain-relevance check in the same node is log-only by default and blocks only when settings.guardrail_block_irrelevant=True (guardrail.py:173-189); that config-gated off-domain interception is a distinct conditional obligation and is not part of this contract's forbidden condition.
Classification is an LLM judge (probabilistic), not deterministic matching; its efficacy is not assessable from source and is not asserted here.

This contract covers only the input-side guardrail; the worker-internal verify_answer anti-hallucination loop is explicitly declared a separate, complementary mechanism (guardrail.py:12-13; supervisor_graph.py:72-94) and is not compiled as an obligation here because no reviewer raised it as one.

Supplied source does not show that chat.py's MainAgent.get_stream actually routes through SupervisorGraph, so application of this guard to the /api/chat and /api/chat/stream requests is not yet bound.
